comment: The Vessel Studio catalog. Amoebius's VESSEL STUDIO page lists these; index.html shows the same studios. Add a studio here and in index.html. Optional accent: the card colour on the hub and the Unity home, a domain key from studio-domains.js (jade, ruby, gold, blue) or a #hex. Optional engineMode: an arcade mode (GameModes name) that PLAY IN ENGINE opens from the main menu in the Amoebius player, the game's own vessel; engineNote says what that run is. "shared": files every studio page loads beside it (studio-look.js = the default graphics, /vessel-studio D19); build_artifact.py publishes them. "mirror": the live mirror, a plain https copy of the same build_artifact.py output (OPEN LIVE IN BROWSER); a mirror of the one artifact in "web", never a second source. Cards (/vessel-studio D35): every surface shows the hub's studio cards. index.html draws them; the native homes (Amoebius's VESSEL STUDIO page, Unity's studio home) draw them from these fields, so they carry the hub's text exactly: "chip", "summary", "spec" (the rows under it), "preview" (a thumbnail of the hub's live canvas, baked by .claude/skills/vessel-studio/bake_previews.cjs), and (no "tuner": Unity has no tuner of its own, D33) on the catalog "lede", "fleet", "fleetNote" and "cardActions": the card's buttons in order, the hosts they work on (web, amoebius, unity) and what a studio needs for one. parity_gate.py fails when these and the hub differ. "newCard": the hub's "+ New studio" card (/vessel-studio D36), its text exactly as the hub shows it; the native homes (Amoebius, Unity) draw it last in their studio grids and open the hub with #<fragment> (the panel).
lede: Pick a vessel and its studio opens: fly it with gamepad, keys or your phone's thumbs, switch its play-style types and element levels, and read what every number does. The same pages open here, in Unity and Amoebius, and in your phone's browser.

cardActions.label: Open studio →
cardActions.tip: The studio, built from this checkout and served (Sync, Ask, Requests and Decisions work), in its own window.

cardActions.label: PLAY IN ENGINE
cardActions.tip: The game's own vessel in Amoebius: builds and starts the game on this studio's mode.

cardActions.label: OPEN LIVE IN BROWSER
cardActions.tip: The published build on the live mirror (GitHub Pages), in your browser.

studios.name: Squirrel
studios.kind: built vessel - studio round 2 (AI sim lab)
studios.summary: The racer, now with an AI sim lab: race AI Squirrels at Easy, Medium or Hard on the game's four Skim Race courses, or hand your hull to the AI and watch with a chase, follow or free camera. Six play-style types over its four element levels.

spec.v: 60 u/s × boost (to 5×)
×1.8 turn, grip 0.25
Charge · Mass · Space · Time

studios.engineNote: The game's own Squirrel in Skim Race, against the shipped AI (pick intensity and AI difficulty on the card).

studios.name: Stoat
studios.kind: design studio - round 28
studios.summary: The slinger. Squeeze a trigger to lay a black-white hole pair and sling round it. Five play styles, momentum carry, a four-level course ladder, an AI sim lab that races every style and scores it, and two modes on T, the game's B: Mass (the field trajectory, a predicted path that boosts you when the poles bend it) and Time (the catch sling, timed at 90°). Its wormhole mode became the Meerkat (2026-10-27). Editor layout with tabs and pop-out windows; touch sticks on a phone.

spec.v: strength 0.5–12 by squeeze
Comet · Needle · Anchor · Maelstrom · Flare
AI pilot · scorecard · cameras
Mass and Time in the game on B; the game still has the Gate too (Ys-bleeding-edge)

studios.engineNote: The game's own Stoat in the Slingshot race (the round-4 orbit sling the game ships today, not the studio's dipole sling).

studios.name: Meerkat
studios.kind: design studio - round 2
studios.summary: The wormhole vessel (the Stoat's Gate mode, made its own vessel). One thumb flies; the grid on your nose is the tunnel RT would form: the right stick bends it up to 120°, shorter and fatter the more it bends, LT shortens it, RT forms it and you ride it, out with the speed you went in with. Only you see the grid, and only while you shape it; everyone sees the formed tunnel as a bridge of spindles over glass and the space round it bent, and its collapse ripples the screen's edges. Every parameter carries its game name (MeerkatWormholeConfig); AI rivals at Easy, Medium or Hard and a level scorecard.

spec.v: the wormhole, on one thumb
bends to 120° · 120–600 u
out at your entry speed
design only: no Meerkat in the game yet

studios.name: Brittle Star
studios.kind: the Unity build - round 4
studios.summary: The Brittle Star as it ships (BrittleStar = 16): a cockpit inside a pentagon of five engines and five guns. Speed (x6), Creation (the slowest, a trail per ring corner), Space (five guns, RT analog, overheating into a danger trail) and Charge (five whip cords that RT stiffens into sabers), and spare rings thrown as a nucleus-wide disk. Demolition Derby and Fauna Frenzy at four intensities, AI rivals at Easy, Medium or Hard flying four element personas, and a scorecard that races every level and style.

spec.v: Cruise · Speed · Creation · Space · Charge
a nucleus-wide disk; a spare per crystal, two at most
one stick · 45 u/s, 270 in Speed
Demolition Derby · Fauna Frenzy

studios.name: Shrike
studios.kind: design studio - round 1
studios.summary: The sniper, from its design document: a very slow one-touch flyer that docks to any block it touches and builds nests to dock in. The Void Lance pierces everything, the Void Sling hurls it to a block in a second, and the Targeting Array sends every nest's missiles at what it paints. Thread the Needle and Den Defense at four intensities, AI Shrikes at Easy, Medium or Hard, and a scorecard with no-sling and no-array controls.

spec.v: one stick · 18 u/s (a proposal)
Lance · Sling · Array · Nest
Thread the Needle · Den Defense
design only: the game's Shrike is a Manta copy

studios.name: Goby and Pistol
studios.kind: crew vessel - in the game
studios.summary: A crew vessel: two seats, one hull, its card reads Goby and Pistol (SO_Vessel.CrewNames, as the Wrasse and Grouper). The Goby flies the 3D world on two thumbs, very fast, and lays the path; the Pistol plays a 2D side view unrolled from that path, rides its hills Tiny Wings style and blows things up. D-pad left or right swaps seats; the AI takes the empty one.

spec.v: two thumbs · 160 u/s · primer · flares
side view · dive · launch · vortex ring · ghost
D-pad left / right · AI in the empty seat
in the Toybox Vessel Changer (not editor-verified)

studios.name: Orca
studios.kind: crew lab - round 9 (Garrett's Crew of Four Lab)
studios.summary: Garrett's 4-seat vessel, in the game as the Orca: a Helm (Time) and three Gunner seats, the sniper (Space), the fast gun (Mass) and the bomb (Charge), each with its own missiles. Take the seats you want; the AI flies the rest. Round 9 adds play styles to choose between while you test: the helm's boost is the Tank, a Breath or the Tide; its shield is the Shield or a Dock; the missiles are flown by wire or are Seekers. Every default is the Orca as it ships.

spec.v: Helm · Sniper · Fast gun · Bomb
Tank / Breath / Tide · Shield / Dock · Fly-by-wire / Seeker
Ring Race · Breach · Anchorage · Broadside
in the Toybox Vessel Changer as the Orca; the round 9 styles are lab-only

studios.name: Siphonophore
studios.kind: voltron vessel designed from the ground up - design lab round 2
studios.summary: One vessel that is three zooids and one colony, taking turns. Apart, the Bell lights the dark crystals, the Sting opens their husks and the Bract nets them into its hold; none of them can score. Fused, the colony digests the hold into the score and rams the walls open, and cannot light, open or catch; the hold empty, it splits itself. Designed from the ground up to alternate, never assembled from vessels that already have a loop.

spec.v: Bell lights · Sting opens · Bract nets (the hold)
Helm rams · Lance opens walls · Ward shields · the hold digests into the score
light, open, net, fuse, digest, split: neither phase can do the other’s work
the Voltron principle (2026-10-27): designed to alternate, not assembled

studios.name: Omega Crews
studios.kind: combiner crew vessels - design lab round 1
studios.summary: Three shipped vessels fly as themselves (their MEGA forms), then gather into one OMEGA form with three seats: Helm flies it, Arms wields the crew’s weapon, Core keeps the shield and the finisher. Swap seats with the arena’s gesture; the AI takes every seat you leave. The omega meter fills apart and drains combined, so you combine for the walls and split for the crystals. Three crews to compare: the Warden (Stoat, Thresher, Butterfly), the Bulwark (Rhino, Grizzly, Scarab), the Tempest (Squirrel, Sparrow, Manta).

spec.v: each member flies its own flight and one RT move
Helm · Arms (weapon) · Core (shield, finisher) · 3 seat
fills on crystals and skims, drains combined; empty = split
Power Rangers SPD: zords, the Megazord, the finisher that ends the fight

studios.name: Gibbon
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind web)
studios.summary: The web-slinger (Yash, 2026-10-18: like Spider-Man). No engine at all: the Gibbon sits still until it shoots a web. The sticks turn it to aim; LT shoots the left hand's web and RT the right's at whatever is near the crosshair (a prism of the course, mass, a rival's trail, a crystal). A web flies out, latches, and is an elastic bungee: hold the trigger and it pulls you in, springy and bouncing; latch off to the side and you swing round the anchor, faster as the web shortens. Let go and you fly on your momentum; shoot the next web before you lose it. Hand over hand, never a thruster.

spec.v: only on its webs: no throttle, no thruster
LT left hand · RT right hand · 220 u, latch on anything
elastic bungee: springy pull, swing, spin-up, bounce off walls
Spider-Man's web swing, without gravity

studios.name: Flea
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind ricochet)
studios.summary: The ricochet. It crawls at 40 u/s on its own; speed comes from bouncing off mass. A hull contact reflects it instead of resetting it, and a press of RT inside the window round the contact is a perfect bounce: ×1.35 and a growing chain. Between bounces it coasts almost ballistically, so you aim the next bounce with the nose. Crouch with LT and release to hop when no mass is near.

spec.v: RT at contact: perfect bounce · LT crouch, release to hop
180 ms, ×1.35 perfect / ×0.85 dull
crawl 40, cap 260 u/s
timing windows and earned speed: Haste, ULTRAKILL, Peglin, parry games

studios.name: Albatross
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind soar)
studios.summary: The soarer. No engine at all: it carries its own ballast, so it falls, and its wings turn speed into lift. Dive to gain speed, pull up to spend it as height, and ride the updraft that rises over every piece of mass (the course ribbon is a thermal corridor). LT spreads the wings for lift and drag, RT folds them for a clean dive. Energy management, not throttle.

spec.v: LT spread (lift) · RT fold (dive) · updrafts over mass
g 10 u/s² (its own; nothing else falls)
glides level at 60, dives to 300 u/s
dive-to-glide: Tears of the Kingdom, Exo One, Sky, the web wings

studios.name: Remora
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind slipstream)
studios.summary: The drafter. Alone it is slow (55 u/s). In a rival's wake its speed cap becomes their speed ×1.3, so it catches anyone it can get behind. Hold LT within reach behind a rival and it latches: towed at their speed, the draft meter filling, taking petals if its Mass is up. Let go, or press RT, and it slings past at ×1.7 their speed plus the draft. Never leads until the last straight.

spec.v: wake draft · LT latch (towed) · release to sling
cap = rival speed ×1.3 within 14 u of their path
×1.7 their speed + draft bonus, 2.5 s
racing's draft and slipstream: Mario Kart World, F-Zero, Rocket League boost chains

studios.name: Dragonfly
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind hover)
studios.summary: The hoverer. The only hull whose velocity has nothing to do with its nose: the left stick thrusts in any direction (strafe, forward, back), the right stick looks, A and B climb and sink, LT stops it dead. RT is a dash: 190 u/s for a quarter second in the direction you are pushing, three pips that regrow, and nothing can touch you mid-dash. Twin-stick arena movement in 3D.

spec.v: left stick thrusts any way · RT dash (3 pips, i-frames) · LT brake
75 u/s, stops in a second
190 u/s × 0.25 s, a pip every 1.2 s
stamina dashes and strafes: Hades II, Silksong, ULTRAKILL, twin-stick arenas

studios.name: Mole
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind burrow)
studios.summary: The burrower. The whole game turned inside out: in open space it is slow (40 u/s) and turns badly; inside mass (within 16 u of any prism) it is fast (150 u/s), turns on a dime, and passes straight through. The course ribbon, the mass beside it, every rival's trail is a highway, and the more others lay, the faster you are. LT digs a tunnel of your own mass for the next lap; RT as you leave mass is a timed breach for a kick.

spec.v: fast inside mass, slow outside · LT dig · RT breach
40 open · 150 inside mass
90°/s open · 220°/s inside
momentum from terrain, inverted: wall-runs, grinds, 'the wall is the fast way'

studios.name: Marlin
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind momentum)
studios.summary: The drifter. Velocity and nose are two different things: the sticks turn the hull freely while it keeps sliding, RT burns along the nose, LT is a retro burn against the velocity, B flips it 180° in a third of a second (flip and burn). A drift assist bends the velocity gently toward the nose so it reads as 3D drifting rather than a physics puzzle; turn it to 0 in Vessel Config for pure Newtonian flight.

spec.v: RT thrust · LT retro · B flip · velocity decoupled
70 u/s², retro 45, cap 220 u/s
1.2/s lateral damping (0 = pure)
3D drift: Chorus's Drift Trance; Squadrons; Everspace 2

studios.name: Eel
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind body)
studios.summary: The body. A head leading a train of segments that follow its exact path: the body IS its trail, shielded mass a rival's hull bounces off. Longer is slower (72 u/s at 8 segments, 45 at 30), and it grows on crystals and skims. LT coils: the turn doubles and the body bunches up behind you; let go and the tail whips straight, cutting any rival or neutral mass it sweeps. RT sheds five segments as standing prisms for a speed burst.

spec.v: LT coil, release to whip · RT shed · the body is the trail
8 → 30 segments, 6 u apart
72 u/s short → 45 u/s long
snake and trail games: Snake.io, Slither, Hole.io (mobile top 10), Tron

studios.name: Octopus
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind pulse)
studios.summary: The pulse jet. Hold LT to inhale: it slows, the mantle swells, the charge fills in 0.7 s. Release and it jets, up to 205 u/s, then fades toward a 20 u/s drift. The beat is yours: release at the same interval as your last two pulses and the chain grows, each pulse ×1.1 more, up to ×1.8. RT spends a pulse of charge on an ink cloud of danger prisms behind you. Charge-and-release movement with a rhythm layer you set yourself.

spec.v: LT inhale, release to jet · your own tempo multiplies · RT ink
55 → 205 u/s by charge, × chain to 1.8
±15% of your last interval
charge-release (Kirby Air Riders, Mario Kart World) + rhythm (Hi-Fi Rush)

studios.name: Gecko
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind surface)
studios.summary: The runner. Hold LT near any mass and it sticks, then runs along the structure: the chain of prisms guides its course, its speed climbs to 130 u/s, the camera rolls onto the surface, and a rival's rail it runs becomes yours. Let go, or press RT, and it hops off with a ×1.4 kick and three seconds of carried momentum to the next surface. Wall-running, where every prismscape is a wall.

spec.v: LT stick and run along mass · release / RT hop
to 130 u/s on a surface, 50 free
×1.4, momentum kept 3 s
wall-running: Titanfall 2, Ghostrunner, Mario Kart World's wall ride

studios.name: Moon Jelly
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind breath)
studios.summary: The breather. One stick steers; one button breathes. Hold it to breathe in: the jelly slows and its bell swells with light. Let go and it pulses forward. Slow, steady breaths (three seconds or more, each like the last) build a calm chain: every pulse glides further and the glow, which is its reach for a crystal, grows wider. Rush and the calm breaks. Calm breaths fill the moon; with the moon full, one long breath lets go into a Moonrise, a glow four times as wide.

spec.v: 1: one stick, one button
hold to breathe in, let go to pulse; slow and steady builds the calm
drifting and breathing / the Moonrise
the Dolphin (charge, then release) + the Butterfly (slow, wide, quiet)

studios.name: Sea Turtle
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind tide)
studios.summary: The wayfinder. It has no throttle: the course line is a tide, a current you can see, and steering into it carries you. Hold the one button to tuck in your flippers and ride the tide fast; let go to spread them, slow down and turn. Out of the tide it only crawls. Where blocks crowd the tide it runs faster: the Rapids. Get through without touching a block and you shoot out with a burst; a bump only slows you a little, because the shell takes it.

spec.v: 1: one stick, one button
the course is a current; hold to tuck in and ride it, let go to turn
gliding the tide / threading the Rapids
the Urchin (latch onto a trail and ride it) + the Squirrel (flow, no hard decisions)

studios.name: Seahorse
studios.kind: concept studio - round 1 (recipe-driven, movement kind tend)
studios.summary: The gardener. Slow and upright. Swim to a plant (any block) and hold the button to curl your tail round it: you stay still, the plant grows a garden round you, and your crystal is called in towards you. Let go and you dart off. A rival coming close is the tense moment: the second button puffs you up, slowing the rival and shielding your garden.

spec.v: 1: one stick, two buttons
hold on to a plant: it grows and calls your crystal in; let go to dart
tending / a rival comes, puff and dart
the Angler (grows plants, leads creatures) + the Serpent (a seed that gathers blocks)

newCard.name: New studio
newCard.summary: Create a vessel or work on one of the fleet: its AI, how it flies, a mini-game of the game or a new one. Name the new ones, say what you want (by voice too), and Claude Code builds it on a new branch.

fleetNote: No studio yet. Press a vessel, or + New studio, to start one; each needs the vessel's own numbers read from its assets first.
